Want to get in touch with Elon Musk, founder and CEO of SpaceX and the co-founder of Tesla? Whether you want to share your thoughts or questions about his products, tell him about your ideas, or just express your appreciation for his work, we've got you covered. Read on for the best ways to reach out to Elon Musk online, by email, or through social media. Prefer to write him a letter? We'll tell you which address to send your mail to so that it reaches Elon.

## How can I contact Elon Musk?

The best way to contact Elon Musk is to email him through one of his companies: Neuralink ([info@neuralink.com](mailto:info@neuralink.com)), SpaceX ([info@spacex.com](mailto:info@spacex.com)), or Tesla ([info@tesla.com](mailto:info@tesla.com)). Or, you can tweet him [@elonmusk](https://x.com/elonmusk).

## Steps

Method 1

Method 1 of 3:

### Contacting Elon Musk via Email or Social Media

 [![PDF download](/extensions/wikihow/socialstamp/images/icon-pdf.svg) Download Article](#)

1. [![Step 1 Email...](https://www.wikihow.com/images/thumb/0/08/Contact-Elon-Musk-Step-2-Version-2.jpg/v4-460px-Contact-Elon-Musk-Step-2-Version-2.jpg)](#/Image:Contact-Elon-Musk-Step-2-Version-2.jpg)

   1

   [**Email**](/Send-Someone-an-Email "Send Someone an Email") **Tesla’s sales or press address.** If you have a question about sales for Elon Musk, you can try contacting him through the Tesla sales email: [NAsales@teslamotors.com](mailto:NAsales@teslamotors.com). If you have a press question or comment for Elon Musk, such as for a news article or story, you can try reaching him through the Tesla press email for North America: [Press@tesla.com](mailto:Press@tesla.com). [[1]](#_note-1) X Research source 
   * You can find a complete list of press email addresses on the [Tesla contact page](https://www.tesla.com/contact).
   * You could also try to contact Musk through the email address of one of his other companies, such as [info@spacex.com](mailto:info@spacex.com) (SpaceX) or [info@neuralink.com](mailto:info@neuralink.com) (Neuralink).
2. 2

   **Contact Musk on X (formerly Twitter).** Elon Musk is active on X and checks his account regularly. You can [tweet him](/Tweet-Someone "Tweet Someone") through his X handle @elonmusk or by accessing his X account [here](https://x.com/elonmusk).[[2]](#_note-2) X Research source  You will need [to create an X account](/Make-a-Twitter-Account "Make a Twitter Account") to tweet at him. To tweet him, write a message on X using 169 characters or less. Include **@elonmusk** in the message so he can be tagged in it and get a notification when you tweet your message.
   * For example, you may tweet, "@elonmusk When can we expect affordable Tesla models for consumers?" or "@elonmusk Thank you for considering the environment when you make your products."[[3]](#_note-3) X Research source
   * He can then respond to you on Twitter by tagging your Twitter handle and posting a message.[[4]](#_note-4) X Research source
   * Consider following Musk on Twitter so you can stay up-to-date on his tweets and connect with him regularly.
   * As of May 2025, Musk does not appear to have a public account on Facebook or Instagram. Previously, Musk could be contacted through the Instagram handle [@elonmusk](https://www.instagram.com/elonmusk/), although this account is now private and no longer verified as belonging to the businessman.
   * ***Be wary of engaging with Facebook or Instagram accounts that are not verified as belonging to Elon Musk. These pages may be run by scammers, so it’s best to avoid any contact with them.***

3. 3

   **Submit a question or comment on the Tesla website.** Use the contact information on the official Tesla website, which can be found [here](https://www.tesla.com/contact). Depending on the reason for your message, you may need to send an email to a certain department or fill out an online form to get in touch with Customer Service.
   * If you want to send a direct message to Tesla’s customer support team at [this link](https://auth.tesla.com/en_us/oauth2/v1/authorize?redirect_uri=https://www.tesla.com/teslaaccount/owner-xp/auth/callback&response_type=code&client_id=ownership&scope=offline_access+openid+ou_code+email+phone&audience=https://ownership.tesla.com/&locale=en-US), you’ll have to sign up for or log in to a Tesla account.
   * If you send a message or email through the Tesla site, include a subject for your message and your comments. Keep the subject line short and to the point so Musk knows what your comments are about.
   * Once you have filled in the form, you can submit it and wait for a response.

results.rawContent:
Looks like Elon Musk is going to have to change his phone number.

The Tesla and SpaceX CEO posted his phone number on Twitter. The tweet was directed at John Carmack, the chief technology officer of Oculus, Facebook's virtual reality subsidiary, but Musk posted it so that anyone could see it.

The tweet was swiftly deleted, but not before it was noticed by many of Musk's 16.7 million Twitter followers.

While Business Insider isn't going to share the number, it does indeed appear to be Musk's personal phone — it registers as ready for Apple iMessage. A reporter at CNBC dialed the number, and found that Musk's "ringing music" is actually a reference to the classic PlayStation game "God of War."

"By the Gods you've done it," the message starts, according to CNBC. "Somehow you've found your way here to me. I offer you my congratulations and my respect."

As for why Musk wanted to talk to Carmack — well, as Carmack later pointed out on Twitter, he's worked in the aerospace industry before, building rockets and founding the non-profit Commercial Spaceflight Federation with Musk back in 2005.

Carmack is primarily known as a video-game industry legend, however, coming to prominence as a cofounder of id Software, the company behind game classics including "Doom" and "Quake." In 2013, Carmack joined Oculus and stayed with the company even after Facebook's purchased it for $2.3 billion in 2014.

Editor's note 12/20/17: This post has been updated to note Carmack's previous background in the aerospace industry.

# Elon Musk accidentally tweets his private phone number

AFP/Getty Images File photo dated 29 September 2017 shows billionaire entrepreneur and founder of SpaceX Elon Musk speaking at the 68th International Astronautical Congress 2017 in Adelaide.

Energy and transport entrepreneur Elon Musk accidentally tweeted his private phone number to his 16.7 million followers on Tuesday. [...] The Tesla and SpaceX CEO divulged the number in what was meant to be a message to John Carmack, head of technology at virtual reality firm Oculus.

"Do you have a sec to talk? My cell is ..." Mr Musk wrote.

The tweet was quickly deleted, but not before many of his followers took note.

TV network CNBC called the number. Instead of getting Mr Musk, CNBC said callers hear a message from the videogame God of War. [...] "By the Gods you've done it," the message begins. "Somehow you've found your way here to me. I offer you my congratulations and my respect."

It is unclear why the South African-born billionaire wanted to talk to Mr Carmack, who joined Oculus in 2013 and stayed with the company after it was acquired by Facebook in 2014.

However, Mr Carmack said in a tweet that he had rocket-building experience and he and Mr Musk had worked together in the past.

# Elon Musk accidentally tweets his private phone number

![](https://static.files.bbci.co.uk/bbcdotcom/web/20261005-153342-40cbc1e8b4-web-3.23.0-2/grey-placeholder.png)
![AFP/Getty Images File photo dated 29 September 2017 shows billionaire entrepreneur and founder of SpaceX Elon Musk speaking at the 68th International Astronautical Congress 2017 in Adelaide.](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/news/480/cpsprodpb/50B3/production/_99295602_hi043311490.jpg.webp)

**Energy and transport entrepreneur Elon Musk accidentally tweeted his private phone number to his 16.7 million followers on Tuesday.**

The Tesla and SpaceX CEO divulged the number in what was meant to be a message to John Carmack, head of technology at virtual reality firm Oculus.

"Do you have a sec to talk? My cell is ..." Mr Musk wrote.

The tweet was quickly deleted, but not before many of his followers took note.

[TV network CNBC called the number](https://www.cnbc.com/2017/12/19/we-called-elon-musks-cell-after-he-accidentally-posted-it-on-twitter.html). Instead of getting Mr Musk, CNBC said callers hear a message from the videogame God of War.

"By the Gods you've done it," the message begins. "Somehow you've found your way here to me. I offer you my congratulations and my respect."

It is unclear why the South African-born billionaire wanted to talk to Mr Carmack, who joined Oculus in 2013 and stayed with the company after it was acquired by Facebook in 2014.

However, Mr Carmack said in a tweet that he had rocket-building experience and he and Mr Musk had worked together in the past.

#### Allow X content?

[A Facebook spokesperson](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2017-12-19/elon-musk-appears-to-have-misfired-direct-message-to-oculus-cto) said Mr Carmack had no plans to leave the company.

Mr Musk's companies work on space travel, electric cars and solar energy.

[In September he unveiled plans for a city-to-city rocket transport system](http://www.bbc.co.uk/news/science-environment-41441877), which could fly people from London to New York in less than half an hour, and for a manned mission to Mars by 2024.
